Users should be able to browse the website, view menus, learn about the private poker room, view events and promotions, and make online reservations or purchases. Use peach puff for container backgrounds and indian red for component visuals.
content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to any single-page navigation pattern where a menu or section link is expected to swap visible content; it does not depend on this bar’s branding or specific menu items.
content.user_trigger: When a visitor clicks the Menu link in the site navigation, the menu section should open and show the bar’s food and drink offerings.
content.verification: Clicking the Menu navigation item should immediately replace the current content with the menu page and show at least one menu item with its description and price.

content.expected_state_change: The page should display a clear introduction to credit repair services, not only a call-to-action or service list.
content.feature_object: the credit repair services introduction section
content.observed_result: After clicking into Services and scrolling several times, the screen kept showing service cards and repeated "Get Started Now" prompts, but no actual introductory explanation of credit repair services appeared.
content.preventative_action: For any services landing section, include a visible introductory block above the CTA that explains what the service is, who it helps, and how the process works. Keep the CTA separate so the page does not rely on action prompts as a substitute for explanatory content.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The services view appears to present only a list of offerings and a consultation CTA, so the page never surfaces a dedicated introductory section for first-time visitors to read.

The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to lead-generation websites and other marketing pages where the primary goal is to present a visible form and service explanation on the landing view.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Load the page and confirm that the first screen already shows a lead form area and a service-information section, with labeled fields and explanatory text visible immediately.

content.expected_state_change: The rendered page visibly satisfies the requested design.
content.feature_object: visible website appearance
content.observed_result: The homepage contains no images, no icons, and no other visual accent elements in the supplied code. The home content is limited to text, one address block, and a four-item services list. The reviewer's note about lacking modern touches matches what the code shows: the page relies entirely on text and colored boxes.
content.preventative_action: Include at least one visible image, icon, or other visual accent in the main page content so the first screen is not only text and plain boxes. Verify that the rendered page shows those elements without requiring navigation or scrolling.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The evidence supports a visible-content limitation on the first screen, not a broken interaction. The page is built without the kinds of visual elements the reviewer named.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a clinical office to display office information and services. The website should have basic pages, including a homepage, about us, services, and contact us. Users should be able to browse the website, learn about the office's information, view the services provided, and contact the office through the contact page. The website should also have a simple navigation menu to help users quickly find the information they need. Style all pages with a light cyan background and cadet blue components.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to informational and service websites that need a first-screen presentation beyond plain text blocks.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Open the homepage and confirm that the first screen includes at least one image, icon, or similar visual accent alongside the text content.

content.expected_state_change: The rendered page visibly satisfies the requested design.
content.feature_object: visible website appearance
content.observed_result: The homepage places the welcome heading, the office information box, and the services box in one column, and both boxes use 2rem padding with 2rem bottom margin. The reviewer still found the space between sections limited and called out the welcome message and information boxes as needing more spacing. The code shows only two stacked content boxes on the homepage, so the spacing complaint is about how tightly those visible sections are separated.
content.preventative_action: Give the welcome area and each information section enough vertical separation and internal padding so the first screen does not feel cramped. Verify that the homepage shows clear gaps between the heading and each content box, with spacing that is easy to see at a glance.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The evidence supports an appearance issue in the first-screen layout, not a functional failure. The sections are present, but their spacing is not generous enough for the reviewer's first-screen reading.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a clinical office to display office information and services. The website should have basic pages, including a homepage, about us, services, and contact us. Users should be able to browse the website, learn about the office's information, view the services provided, and contact the office through the contact page. The website should also have a simple navigation menu to help users quickly find the information they need. Style all pages with a light cyan background and cadet blue components.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to landing pages and homepages that present a welcome area followed by stacked information panels or cards.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Render the homepage and check that the welcome heading, office information section, and services section are separated by visibly larger vertical gaps and padding.

content.expected_state_change: The rendered page visibly satisfies the requested design.
content.feature_object: visible website appearance
content.observed_result: The home view renders the heading "Welcome to Credit Repair Experts" inside a page whose app container uses `background-color: oldlace`. The main content cards use white backgrounds, while the navigation and buttons use `background-color: rosybrown` with white text. The reviewer reported that the text-to-background contrast is very low, that the typography is minimal, and that the text, buttons, and backgrounds could use more variation or contrast.
content.preventative_action: Make the main heading and primary copy use a clearly readable text color and weight against the page background, and ensure buttons and surrounding sections have enough contrast to stand apart from each other. Verify that the first screen has legible text and visibly distinct text, button, and background treatments without relying on scrolling.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The code shows the page copy and controls are present, but the first-screen styling does not give the heading and UI enough contrast against the light background. This is an appearance issue about readability and visual distinction on the initial view.

The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to lead-generation landing pages and other single-page marketing sites that rely on a hero heading, navigation buttons, and section cards.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Render the first screen and check that the main heading and body copy are easy to read at a glance, and that buttons are visually distinct from nearby sections.

content.expected_state_change: The rendered page visibly satisfies the requested design.
content.feature_object: visible website appearance
content.observed_result: The home view has a "Get My Free Credit Score" button, and the services view and home view both use "Get Started Now"-style calls to action. The reviewer said the button design is decent but not visually prominent enough to grab attention.
content.preventative_action: Style the primary call-to-action so it is clearly the most prominent button on the page, with a distinct visual treatment that makes it easy to spot at a glance. Verify that the main CTA stands out from secondary buttons and nearby content when the page first loads.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The code shows the call-to-action buttons are present, but they use the same rosybrown styling as other UI elements and do not stand out strongly from the surrounding sections. This is an appearance issue about button prominence, not absence or non-response.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a credit repair company to generate leads. The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to landing pages, lead forms, and other sites that depend on one primary action button.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Check the rendered page and confirm that the primary CTA is immediately noticeable compared with other buttons and section elements.

content.expected_state_change: The page should show the full service explanations in a visible, readable section so the visitor can review what each service includes.
content.feature_object: the credit repair services information section
content.observed_result: The tester clicked into the Services section and then kept scrolling, but the detailed service content was still not visible before the interaction budget ran out.
content.preventative_action: For any informational section, render the full text in the initial viewport or provide a clear in-page anchor that jumps directly to the detailed content. Avoid burying essential service descriptions behind excessive scrolling or ambiguous layout spacing.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The services content appears to be placed lower on the page or otherwise not surfaced clearly enough for a first-time visitor to review within the available interactions; the run ended before the tester could reach a concrete defect beyond incomplete visibility.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a credit repair company to generate leads. The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.
content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to websites that present service explanations or marketing copy in a dedicated section; it does not address forms, score lookups, or styling choices.
content.user_trigger: When a visitor opens the services area, they should be able to read the company’s credit repair service descriptions without needing extra steps or hidden navigation.
content.verification: Open the Services section and confirm that all service descriptions are immediately visible or reachable through a single, obvious jump link, with no need for repeated scrolling to find the actual text.

content.expected_state_change: The page should switch from the home view to a visible menu view with item names, descriptions, and prices.
content.feature_object: the menu navigation feature that opens the menu content page
content.observed_result: After clicking the "Menu" link repeatedly and waiting, the page stayed on an empty or unchanged content area and never displayed the menu items, descriptions, or prices.
content.preventative_action: For any tabbed or link-driven view switcher, render the selected view component in the main content area and make sure each navigation control updates the active state that controls what is shown. If a menu link is present, it must be connected to an actual menu panel rather than a placeholder click handler.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The navigation action appears to be wired to a view state, but the menu view is not actually rendered into the main content area, so the click has no visible effect for a visitor.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for The All-In Bourbon Bar to showcase its products and services. The website should have functionalities for displaying menus, introducing the membership-only private poker room, and showcasing events and promotions. Users should be able to browse the website, view menus, learn about the private poker room, view events and promotions, and make online reservations or purchases. Use peach puff for container backgrounds and indian red for component visuals.
content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to any single-page navigation pattern where a menu or section link is expected to swap visible content; it does not depend on this bar’s branding or specific menu items.
content.user_trigger: When a visitor clicks the Menu link in the site navigation, the menu section should open and show the bar’s food and drink offerings.
content.verification: Clicking the Menu navigation item should immediately replace the current content with the menu page and show at least one menu item with its description and price.

content.expected_state_change: The events and promotions page should become visible, showing upcoming events and related promotional content instead of leaving the page blank.
content.feature_object: the top navigation’s Events link should open the events and promotions section
content.observed_result: Clicking the Events link multiple times did not reveal any events content; the page stayed blank aside from the navigation bar, and the tester ultimately answered NO.
content.preventative_action: For any tab or link-based navigation, connect the control to a real view switch or route change and render the target section immediately after activation. If the page uses conditional views, include the destination component in the render tree and verify the click updates the visible content rather than only emitting an event.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The Events navigation action appears not to be wired to a rendered view, so the click does not actually change the displayed content. The evaluator log only shows a driver list-index error after repeated attempts, so the concrete visible defect is that the events section never appeared.

content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The services view appears to present only a list of offerings and a consultation CTA, so the page never surfaces a dedicated introductory section for first-time visitors to read.

task: Please create a software solutions website to provide information to prospective customers. Use peach puff for container backgrounds and indian red for component visuals.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to landing pages and brochure sites that use boxed sections for featured content, menus, services, or promotions.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Open the rendered page and check that each main container displays at least one visible heading and body block immediately on load, with no empty white boxes dominating the screen.

content.expected_state_change: The rendered page visibly satisfies the requested design.
content.feature_object: visible website appearance
content.observed_result: The reviewer said the typography is functional but basic. The code uses the default Inter/system font stack in :root, sets h1 to 3.2em, and otherwise relies on the base browser text styling for most content. The homepage sections are mostly plain headings, paragraphs, and buttons.
content.preventative_action: Apply a consistent typographic system with clearly differentiated heading and body styles, and verify that the first screen shows those text styles across the main sections. Check that headings, labels, and body text are intentionally styled rather than left at default-looking settings.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The first-screen text is readable but minimally styled, so the visible-side issue is that the typography does not carry much visual distinction.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a solar company to display company information and products. The website should have functionalities for company introduction, product showcase, news updates, and contact us. Users should be able to browse the company's history, mission, and values, view detailed product information, learn about the company's latest news and events, and contact the company through the contact page with name, email and message. Use lemon chiffon in the background layer and chocolate for the component layer.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to informational websites and marketing pages that rely on text-heavy sections.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Inspect the rendered page and confirm that headings, body text, and labels use distinct, deliberate typography styles.

content.expected_state_change: The selected section should replace the homepage content with visible page content for that destination, rather than leaving the content area blank.
content.feature_object: page navigation to the company information sections
content.observed_result: Clicking About Us, Products, News, and Contact changed the active tab, but the page content area stayed empty in the screenshots; only the top navigation and background were visible.
content.preventative_action: For any tabbed or menu-driven site, wire each navigation state to a real rendered panel or routed page component, and make sure inactive states still show a visible fallback or placeholder instead of an empty main area. If the page uses conditional rendering, every menu option should map to a mounted component with content and not just update state.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The app only renders the home view in the main content area, while the other tabs have no implemented page components, so navigation switches to states that display nothing. The evaluator log also ended with a driver index error after those clicks, but the concrete UI issue visible in the trajectory is that the destination pages were not rendered.

content.observed_result: The page uses the default-looking Inter/system-ui/Avenir/Helvetica/Arial/sans-serif stack in :root, and the body also sets Arial, sans-serif. The reviewer called the font choice and hierarchy dated, and the code shows no separate display font or stronger heading system beyond the shared h1, h2, h3 color rule.
content.preventative_action: Use a distinct typography system with a clearly differentiated heading scale and body text style, and verify that headings, subheadings, and paragraph text are visually separated on the first screen.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The visible typography is driven by the current font stack and heading styling, so the dated feel is an appearance issue in the first-screen presentation rather than a missing feature.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a solar company to display company information and products. The website should have functionalities for company introduction, product showcase, news updates, and contact us. Users should be able to browse the company's history, mission, and values, view detailed product information, learn about the company's latest news and events, and contact the company through the contact page with name, email and message. Use lemon chiffon in the background layer and chocolate for the component layer.
content.transfer_limits: Applies to marketing, company, and product websites that rely on text hierarchy for first-screen presentation.
content.user_trigger: View the rendered page
content.verification: Render the page and check that the main title, section headings, and body copy use clearly different sizes/weights and a deliberate font choice instead of a single default-looking stack.

content.expected_state_change: The page should show the full service explanations in a visible, readable section so the visitor can review what each service includes.
content.feature_object: the credit repair services information section
content.observed_result: The tester clicked into the Services section and then kept scrolling, but the detailed service content was still not visible before the interaction budget ran out.
content.preventative_action: For any informational section, render the full text in the initial viewport or provide a clear in-page anchor that jumps directly to the detailed content. Avoid burying essential service descriptions behind excessive scrolling or ambiguous layout spacing.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The services content appears to be placed lower on the page or otherwise not surfaced clearly enough for a first-time visitor to review within the available interactions; the run ended before the tester could reach a concrete defect beyond incomplete visibility.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for a credit repair company to generate leads. The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.
content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to websites that present service explanations or marketing copy in a dedicated section; it does not address forms, score lookups, or styling choices.
content.user_trigger: When a visitor opens the services area, they should be able to read the company’s credit repair service descriptions without needing extra steps or hidden navigation.
content.verification: Open the Services section and confirm that all service descriptions are immediately visible or reachable through a single, obvious jump link, with no need for repeated scrolling to find the actual text.

content.expected_state_change: The selected news item should expand or navigate to a readable article detail view instead of leaving the user on the same list with only the teaser excerpt.
content.feature_object: Browsing news articles and opening an article’s full details from the News section
content.observed_result: On the News page, clicking "Read More" for the "Industry Partnership" article did not reveal any article detail view; the screen stayed on the same list of excerpts and the tester kept clicking the same control until the interaction budget was exhausted.
content.preventative_action: For any article list, make each teaser’s "Read More" control either route to a dedicated detail page or open a populated detail panel/modal with the full article content. The control must change the visible state after activation so users can tell the article opened.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The page appears to render only a static news list with teaser text and a non-navigating "Read More" button, so there is no implemented article-detail interaction for the tester to reach. The cause is established by the trajectory and the visible UI, not by a page error.
content.task_requirement: Please create a software solutions website to provide information to prospective customers. The website should have content that introduces software solutions and staffing business, including product and service descriptions, industry news and trends, customer cases and success stories, etc. The website should be able to attract the attention of small to medium-sized businesses, and the content should be easy to understand and engaging. Users should be able to browse the website, search for relevant information or product descriptions, read articles and news, and contact the website owner for more information. Configure all backgrounds with misty rose and all components with firebrick.
content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to any list of articles, announcements, or posts that advertises a deeper read-more action; it does not depend on this site’s business domain.
content.user_trigger: When a user clicks a news article’s "Read More" control, the site should open that article’s detailed view so the user can read the full story and any supporting details.
content.verification: Open the News section and activate a "Read More" control; the page should visibly change to show the full article content or a dedicated article detail view.

content.expected_state_change: The page should display a clear introduction to credit repair services, not only a call-to-action or service list.
content.feature_object: the credit repair services introduction section
content.observed_result: After clicking into Services and scrolling several times, the screen kept showing service cards and repeated "Get Started Now" prompts, but no actual introductory explanation of credit repair services appeared.
content.preventative_action: For any services landing section, include a visible introductory block above the CTA that explains what the service is, who it helps, and how the process works. Keep the CTA separate so the page does not rely on action prompts as a substitute for explanatory content.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The services view appears to present only a list of offerings and a consultation CTA, so the page never surfaces a dedicated introductory section for first-time visitors to read.

content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to any marketing site where a navigation target is meant to educate visitors before conversion; it does not depend on credit repair specifically.
content.user_trigger: When a visitor opens the services area of the site, they should be able to read an introductory explanation of the credit repair services offered.
content.verification: Open the services section and confirm that an introductory paragraph or section is visible immediately, before or alongside the service cards and CTA.

content.expected_state_change: The website should show a dedicated customer cases or success stories section with readable example stories or case-study details.
content.feature_object: Customer cases and success stories content
content.observed_result: The tester explored the visible Services, News, and Contact pages, but none of them showed any customer cases or success stories; the News page only contained generic articles like 'New Product Launch' and 'Industry Partnership'.
content.preventative_action: Provide a dedicated, reachable customer cases or success stories section or page, and include it in the main navigation or another obvious entry point. Populate it with actual case-study content instead of only generic product, service, or news summaries.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The site appears to have no dedicated customer cases or success stories content or entry point, so the tester could not find the required information anywhere they looked.

content.verification: Open the site and navigate through the main menu to a customer cases or success stories page; confirm that it displays at least one concrete story or case study rather than only general marketing copy.

content.expected_state_change: The site should show reachable navigation entries or content sections for software solutions, industry news, customer cases/success stories, and contact information.
content.feature_object: website navigation and content sections for software solutions information
content.observed_result: The tester found only Home, Products, Services, News, and Contact in the navigation. They looked through those visible sections, but there was no dedicated Software Solutions section and no Customer Stories / customer cases / success stories section anywhere they reached.
content.preventative_action: Provide a distinct, reachable navigation entry or routed section for each required content area, including a dedicated software-solutions page and a customer-stories/case-studies page. content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The required content structure is incomplete: the site exposes Products/Services/News/Contact, but it does not provide separate, reachable sections for Software Solutions and Customer Stories. The run also ended with an interaction-budget exhaustion before any hidden or alternate entry point was found.

content.expected_state_change: The page must show a reservation form or a successful reservation confirmation after the RSVP action, instead of staying on the event cards with no follow-up state change.
content.feature_object: event RSVP actions should open a reservation flow for an event
content.observed_result: Clicking the RSVP buttons on the Events & Promotions cards did not open any reservation form or confirmation; the screen stayed on the same event listing with the RSVP buttons visible.
content.preventative_action: For any RSVP or booking control, wire the button to a real interaction path: open a form, modal, or routed checkout/reservation view, and render a visible success state after submission. A static button should never be the only affordance for an action that is supposed to create a reservation.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The RSVP control appears to be a static button with no click handler or reservation UI attached, so the interaction does not change page state. The cause is established by the trajectory and the rendered component showing only a plain button.
content.task_requirement: Please implement a website for The All-In Bourbon Bar to showcase its products and services. The website should have functionalities for displaying menus, introducing the membership-only private poker room, and showcasing events and promotions. Users should be able to browse the website, view menus, learn about the private poker room, view events and promotions, and make online reservations or purchases. Use peach puff for container backgrounds and indian red for component visuals.
content.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to any event RSVP, booking, or purchase button that is meant to start an online reservation flow; it does not address unrelated navigation or content display features.
content.user_trigger: When a user clicks an RSVP button for an event or promotion, the site should present a reservation form or otherwise advance into a reservation flow that can be completed online.
content.verification: Click each RSVP control and confirm that the UI changes to a reservation form or confirmation message without requiring repeated clicks.

content.expected_state_change: Submitting the completed form should switch the page from the input fields to a thank-you/confirmation state that tells the user their information was received.
content.feature_object: lead submission form
content.observed_result: The tester filled the personal information fields and selected a credit issue, but the run ended before the submit button was clicked, so no confirmation state was observed.
content.preventative_action: For any multi-step form, keep the submit control reachable within the interaction budget and make the confirmation state appear immediately after a successful submit event. If the form is meant to be tested end-to-end, avoid requiring extra navigation or hidden steps before the final submission action.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The check ran out of interaction budget before the final submit action, so the form’s post-submit behavior was not exercised.

content.user_trigger: When a visitor fills in the lead form with valid personal and credit-status information and submits it, the site should record the submission and show a confirmation message.
content.verification: Fill every required field with valid values, click the submit button, and confirm that the form is replaced by a visible success message or receipt state.

content.expected_state_change: Submitting a valid vote should briefly display a confirmation message or notification on the voting view.
content.feature_object: vote submission feedback after casting a poll vote
content.observed_result: The tester selected an option and clicked Submit Vote, and the option count increased, but no visible confirmation notification appeared; the run ended after repeated attempts with the same missing feedback.
content.preventative_action: For any vote-submit control, render a clear success message in the same view immediately after a valid submission and keep it visible long enough for a user to read. If the confirmation is transient, make it accessible through a persistent status area or toast region rather than relying on a momentary flash.
content.root_cause_or_hypothesis: The voting control updates the option count but the confirmation feedback is either not rendered, not visible long enough, or not reached during the interaction budget; the evaluator log only shows the driver stopping with an unknown action, so the concrete defect is the missing visible confirmation after submission.

content.user_trigger: When a user selects a poll option and submits their vote, the page should show a visible confirmation that the vote was recorded.
